newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks soar; Tokyo, London also post gains.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks soar; Tokyo, London also post gains.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.

LONDON - British shares ended higher, but well off their record peaks set earlier after an early burst of buying on Wall Street faded. Surging U.S. stocks propelled the benchmark FTSE 100 to an intraday record at 4,100 briefly before slowly giving back gains. The index ended 26.3 points higher at 4,077.6, rising 105.2 from last Friday.

FRANKFURT - German shares end bourse dealings strongly ahead, powered by overnight gains on Wall Street and in U.S. Treasuries, which also boosted German Bunds. Settlement of DAX future contracts and last trading day for constituent stock options also helps gains. The 30-share DAX index ended up 46.70 points, or 1.66 percent, at 2,854.45 points, up 54.74 on a week ago. In post-bourse trade the index was up 10.71 at 2,835.54.

PARIS - French shares closed with a jump of more than 1 percent in heavy turnover, tracking the "Santa Claus rally" on Wall Street. "The big push was today before people head for the hills, said a senior equity salesman, referring to departures for the Christmas week holiday. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 29.83 points, or 1.33 percent, at 2,278.53 a gain of 75.12 on last Friday.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed slightly higher but near the sessions lows, giving up some gains despite a firmer Wall Street opening. Attention centred on CS Holding and Electrowatt. The all share Swiss Performance Index rose 5.92 points, 0.24 percent, to end at 2,481.68 up 27 since last week.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed moderately higher after a volatile session, with the key market index rising 0.61 percent. But brokers said the market, which had fallen sharply on Thursday, was still basically on a downward trend due to disappointment at the government's handling of the economy. The benchmark Nikkei 225 average closed up 119.79 points, or 0.61 percent, at 19,690.46, a drop of 650.93 from last Friday.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong's Hang Seng index posted its biggest point gain in more than two years, charging to a sharply higher close as investors cheered a drop in U.S. bond yields and a surge in Wall Street stocks overnight. The Hang Seng Index surged 284.85 points, or 2.22 percent, to close at 13,131.41 a rise of 347.34 on the week.

SYDNEY - Australian shares sprinted home in the afternoon to close sharply higher as strong buying interest late in the day ensured a positive response to the Dow's second-biggest point gain ever. The All Ordinaries index jumped 42.1 points to close at 2,373.8, up 57.3 from last Friday.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks raced to their third succesive rise on Friday as major world stock markets surged upward ahead of the festive season. The all-share index closed up 72.4 points to 6,540.4, up 57.9 from last week. Industrials jumped 71.1 points to end at 7,795.8. This was up 113.3 since last Friday. Gold shares were buoyed by a firmer bullion price in European markets and the gold index put on a tentative 10.6 points to 1,501.9, down 9.7 on the week.
